object.name: evi_freqshift_hilbert
object.digest: Time-domain Hilbert frequency shifter effect with three simultaneous sidebands outputs
object.description: Like MSP <o>freqshift~</o> but with a different hilbert filter and additional features, such as antialiased saturation and automatic clickless phase reset. If using in gen~ alone the samplerate must be 48kHz, or if running at a different samplerate the hilbert filter coefficients must be fed in externally. See the <o>evi.freqshift.hilbert~</o> abstraction for an example. For a frequency shifter that does not require external coefficients see <o>evi_freqshift_weaver</o>.gendsp.

inlets.name: frequency
inlets.digest: float/int/signal. If float/int, frequency shift in Hz +/- 0. (use @freqsmooth attribute to smooth).

inlets.name: frequency
inlets.digest: + audio rate FM of freq shift amount ± Hz.

inlets.name: signal
inlets.digest: Has the same effect (but sample accurate) as sending 'resetphase' to the MSP 'freqshift~' object - it resets the phase of the quadrature oscillators that modulate the sidebands of the incoming signal. Note that in 'evi_freqshift_hilbert' this inlet need not be used, as a major feature of the internal gen~ code is that it does automatic and clickless resetting of phase itself (depending on the @resetauto attribute, which is on by default).

outlets.name: sidebands
outlets.digest: Sidebands mixed and optionally saturated (use @bandsmix attribute and @drive attribute).

outlets.name: quad
outlets.digest: Quad Osc Cos. This can be useful for synchronising downstream processing.

outlets.name: quad
outlets.digest: Quad Osc Sin. This can be useful for synchronising downstream processing.

outlets.name: sync
outlets.digest: Osc Sync Phase 0..1, this can be useful for synchronising downstream processing.

attributes.name: bandsmix
attributes.description: Normalised 0..1, mix the far left outlet between 0 = Upper (or positive) and 1 = Lower (or negative) SideBands. Smoothed by the @smooth attribute.

attributes.name: coef1
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 1

attributes.name: coef2
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 2

attributes.name: coef3
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 3

attributes.name: coef4
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 4

attributes.name: coef5
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 5

attributes.name: coef6
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 6

attributes.name: coef7
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 7

attributes.name: coef8
attributes.description: Polyphase IIR Halfband Allpass Cascade Coefficient 8

attributes.name: drive
attributes.description: If the @saturation attribute is set to on (1), @drive adds gain shaping to the internal sine shaping saturation algorithm. This affects the far left bands mixing outlet but not the separately avilable USB and LSB outlets.

attributes.name: freqsmooth
attributes.description: Smoothing amount in ms for the frequency shifting 2nd inlet. Because FM signal rate control (inlet 3) is merged with the smoothed freq shift amount after this smoothing factor, the smoothing need not be turned off (0) when using audio rate FM if not wished for.

attributes.name: resetauto
attributes.description: Flag 0/1, if set to on (1, default), phase resetting of the internal quadrature oscillators happens automatically and clicklessly. If set to off (0), 'evi_freqshift_hilbert' behaves like MSP 'freqshift~' and requires resetting the phase via inlet 4, which clicks.

attributes.name: saturation
attributes.description: Flag 0/1, turn the internal saturation off (0) or on (1). This saturation is a sine shaping waveshaper that is controlled by the @drive attribute. It is only applied to the far left bands mix outlet.

attributes.name: smooth
attributes.description: Smooth time in ms of the internal parameters. Note that the freq shift (inlet 2) has it's own independent smoothing attribute (@freqsmooth).
